THOUGHT: The patient has progressive, symmetric proximal muscle weakness (difficulty climbing stairs, brushing hair) with elevated muscle enzymes (CK, aldolase) and EMG changes consistent with an inflammatory myopathy. Muscle biopsy shows endomysial infiltration by CD8+ T lymphocytes, which is characteristic of polymyositis. Dermatomyositis would usually have a characteristic rash and perifascicular atrophy with perivascular/CD4+ infiltrates. Inclusion body myositis typically occurs in older patients (>50), often has distal/asymmetric weakness and rimmed vacuoles on biopsy. Other causes (myasthenia gravis, metabolic or drug-induced myopathies) are less consistent with the biopsy and laboratory findings. These findings together most strongly indicate polymyositis (an idiopathic inflammatory myopathy mediated by CD8+ T cells).

DIAGNOSIS: Polymyositis
